$comment: Generated by scripts/build-mcp-catalog.mjs from the tools/list payload of every three.ws MCP server and the price maps in this repo. Do not edit by hand: npm run build:mcp-catalog regenerates it and npm run audit:mcp-catalog fails the build when it is stale.

census.method: Computed, never typed: each hosted endpoint is counted by importing the exact catalog, resource table and prompt set it serves, and each stdio package by loading its server in-process and calling tools/list, resources/list and prompts/list over an in-memory MCP transport. tools: every tool an endpoint can serve, including financial-tier tools the policy hides until a session enables them (defaultOn is what a fresh session sees). resources: fixed-URI resources/list entries. templates: resources/templates/list entries. prompts: prompts/list entries rendered against that endpoint's own catalog. unique: distinct tool names across all servers. /api/mcp-chatgpt and /api/mcp-grok serve subsets of /api/mcp-studio, so per-server figures overlap and unique is the headline total. Recomputed on every build (public/mcp-catalog.json, public/tools.json) and on every request to /api/mcp-census; npm run check:mcp-counts fails the gate when a doc quotes a number that no longer matches.

tools.name: getting_started
tools.title: Getting Started (free)
tools.description: FREE, start here. Returns an overview of the three.ws MCP server: every tool and what it does, how to access it, and useful links. No payment or account required. Call this first to orient.
tools.whenToUse: Call this first to orient.

section.description: Which part to return. Defaults to "overview" (everything). Use "tools", "access", or "links" to focus.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.title: Search the three.ws asset catalog
tools.description: FREE, no account or payment. Search every ready-made asset three.ws publishes in one call: CC0 3D props and objects, rigged humanoid characters, and retargetable motion clips. Returns ids, titles, tags, licenses, and CDN urls, plus category facets to narrow the next query. Use this before generating anything: if the catalog already has the prop or character, dropping it in is instant and free where generating one is not. Feed a returned id to get_item_source for code that renders it on any site.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before generating anything: if the catalog already has the prop or character, dropping it in is instant and free where generating one is not.

q.description: Free text over titles, names, tags, and categories, e.g. "wooden chair", "office", "wave". Every word must match somewhere, so start broad.

kind.description: Narrow to one library: object (CC0 props), character (rigged humanoids), animation (motion clips).

category.description: Exact category from a previous result's facets.

tag.description: Exact tag from a previous result's facets.

offset.description: Page offset. Use next_offset from the previous response.

tools.name: get_catalog_item
tools.title: Read one catalog item
tools.description: FREE, no account or payment. Read one three.ws catalog item in full by its id from search_catalog (for example "object:adjustable_wrench"): metadata, license, CDN urls, the site links that preview or edit it, related items of the same kind, and which source frameworks get_item_source can emit for it. Use this after search_catalog to inspect one result before you embed it; for paste-ready code call get_item_source instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after search_catalog to inspect one result before you embed it; for paste-ready code call get_item_source instead.

id.description: Catalog id as `<kind>:<name>` from search_catalog. A bare name is also accepted.

tools.name: get_item_source
tools.title: Get paste-ready source for a catalog item
tools.description: FREE, no account or payment. Returns working code that renders one three.ws catalog item on any site: the <agent-3d> web component (pinned to the exact published version with its SRI hash), the <model-viewer> tag our own browse grids use, plain three.js with GLTFLoader, or a React component. Motion clips return three.js code that parses the clip JSON and plays it. Omit `framework` to get the one that fits the item best; pass `all` to get every variant at once. Use this when you are ready to put a catalog item on a page or in an app; call get_catalog_item first if you still need its license or metadata.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you are ready to put a catalog item on a page or in an app; call get_catalog_item first if you still need its license or metadata.

id.description: Catalog id from search_catalog.

framework.description: Which form to emit. Defaults to the recommended one for the item kind. "all" returns every applicable variant.

tools.name: list_my_avatars
tools.title: List my avatars
tools.description: List the authenticated user's avatars. Returns id, name, slug, size, visibility, and direct model_url (when visibility permits). Use this to find the id of an avatar you already own before rendering, embedding, or attaching it to an agent; to browse other people's avatars call search_public_avatars instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find the id of an avatar you already own before rendering, embedding, or attaching it to an agent; to browse other people's avatars call search_public_avatars instead.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from previous response.

tools.name: get_avatar
tools.title: Get avatar
tools.description: Fetch a single avatar by id or by owner+slug. Returns metadata and a model_url (public/unlisted) or short-lived signed URL (private). Use this when you already have an avatar id or owner+slug and need its model_url or metadata; to find ids call list_my_avatars or search_public_avatars.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you already have an avatar id or owner+slug and need its model_url or metadata; to find ids call list_my_avatars or search_public_avatars.

tools.name: search_public_avatars
tools.title: Search public avatars
tools.description: Search the public avatar gallery. Use this to find characters to render when you do not already know an avatar id; for your own avatars call list_my_avatars instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find characters to render when you do not already know an avatar id; for your own avatars call list_my_avatars instead.

q.description: Free-text search over name and description.

tools.name: render_avatar
tools.title: Render avatar
tools.description: Produce an HTML <model-viewer> snippet that renders the given avatar. Return this text as an inline HTML artifact to display an interactive 3D avatar. Use this when the user wants to see and rotate an avatar inline; for a flat image file call render_avatar_image, and for a snippet to paste on another site call get_embed_code.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the user wants to see and rotate an avatar inline; for a flat image file call render_avatar_image, and for a snippet to paste on another site call get_embed_code.

poster.description: Optional poster image URL shown while loading.

tools.name: render_avatar_image
tools.title: Render an avatar to an image
tools.description: Render a stored avatar to a real PNG/JPEG/WebP image (headless three.js) and return its URL - ready for an tag, social card, or game loader. Choose a camera framing (scene), an optional pose preset and ARKit-52 expression. Renders are cached, so repeat calls with the same parameters return instantly. Works on your own avatars (any visibility) and on public avatars. Use this when you need a still image rather than an interactive viewer; for a live 3D view call render_avatar.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you need a still image rather than an interactive viewer; for a live 3D view call render_avatar.

pose.description: Optional pose preset id (see pose_model / the render catalog).

tools.name: delete_avatar
tools.title: Delete avatar
tools.description: Soft-delete an avatar you own. Requires avatars:delete scope. Use this when the user explicitly asks to remove one of their avatars; confirm which one with get_avatar first.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the user explicitly asks to remove one of their avatars; confirm which one with get_avatar first.

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm permanent deletion.

tools.name: get_embed_code
tools.title: Get embed code
tools.description: Return a ready-to-paste <iframe> embed snippet (plus shareable URL, oEmbed URL, and OG thumbnail) for a three.ws avatar, on-chain agent, or Forge creation. Embed a persistent 3D avatar into Notion, Webflow, Framer, a blog, or any site as easily as a YouTube video. Provide exactly one target: agent_id, OR chain_id + onchain_agent_id, OR creation_id. Use this when the user wants to show an avatar, agent, or creation on a site they control; for an embed that only token holders can view call create_gated_embed instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the user wants to show an avatar, agent, or creation on a site they control; for an embed that only token holders can view call create_gated_embed instead.

agent_id.description: Embed a regular three.ws agent.

chain_id.description: EVM chain id of an on-chain (ERC-8004) agent.

onchain_agent_id.description: Token id of the on-chain agent (pair with chain_id).

ar.description: Offer an AR / view-in-room button on mobile.

tools.name: create_gated_embed
tools.title: Create a token-gated embed
tools.description: Turn an avatar or on-chain agent you own into a holder-only interactive 3D embed. Visitors must prove, with a real, server-verified Solana SPL token balance and never a client-reported number, that they hold at least min_amount of mint before the live scene renders; below that they see a designed locked teaser with a connect-wallet CTA. mint defaults to $THREE but accepts any SPL mint at runtime. Returns a ready-to-paste <three-d> embed snippet. Use this when the embed should render only for holders of a token; for an open embed anyone can see call get_embed_code.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the embed should render only for holders of a token; for an open embed anyone can see call get_embed_code.

asset_id.description: The embed asset to gate: "avatar:<uuid>" or "<chainId>:<agentId>" (on-chain agent you own).

mint.description: SPL token mint holders must have a balance of. Defaults to $THREE (FeMbDoX7R1Psc4GEcvJdsbNbZA3bfztcyDCatJVJpump). Pass a different mint to gate with another community's token.

min_amount.description: Minimum token balance a visitor must hold to unlock the embed.

tools.name: validate_model
tools.title: Validate glTF/GLB model
tools.description: Run the Khronos glTF-Validator against a remote GLB or glTF URL. Returns a structured report of errors, warnings, infos, and hints: the authoritative answer to "is this file spec-compliant?". SSRF-hardened: only public https URLs are fetched. Use this before shipping, minting, or embedding a model to catch spec errors; for size and structure stats call inspect_model.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before shipping, minting, or embedding a model to catch spec errors; for size and structure stats call inspect_model.

url.description: Public https URL of a .glb or .gltf file.

tools.name: inspect_model
tools.title: Inspect glTF/GLB model
tools.description: Parse a remote GLB or glTF and return structural stats: scene/node/mesh counts, vertex and triangle totals, material and texture summaries, extensions used. Pure inspection, no optimization advice. Use this to learn what a model contains; for ways to make it smaller call optimize_model, and for spec errors call validate_model.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to learn what a model contains; for ways to make it smaller call optimize_model, and for spec errors call validate_model.

url.description: Public https URL of a .glb or .gltf file.

tools.name: optimize_model
tools.title: Suggest optimizations for a glTF/GLB model
tools.description: Inspect the model and return actionable suggestions for reducing size and draw-call overhead: triangle budget, Draco/Meshopt compression, oversized textures, KTX2 transcoding, non-indexed primitives, redundant materials, and more. Use this when a model is too heavy to load quickly on the web or on mobile; for raw counts without advice call inspect_model.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when a model is too heavy to load quickly on the web or on mobile; for raw counts without advice call inspect_model.

url.description: Public https URL of a .glb or .gltf file.

tools.name: diff_models
tools.title: Diff two glTF/GLB models
tools.description: Compare two remote GLB or glTF models and return what changed: geometry, hierarchy, materials, textures, skeletons, and animation clips, each classified as added, removed, renamed, moved, or modified, with renames detected by content hash rather than by name. Every change carries a severity (none, cosmetic, minor, major, breaking) so an agent can decide whether an optimized, rigged, or re-exported model is still safe to ship. Breaking means something a consumer references by name is gone: a clip, a joint, a mesh. Use this after optimizing, rigging, or re-exporting a model to confirm the new version is still safe wherever the old one was used.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after optimizing, rigging, or re-exporting a model to confirm the new version is still safe wherever the old one was used.

before.description: Public https URL of the baseline .glb or .gltf file.

after.description: Public https URL of the candidate .glb or .gltf file.

tools.name: print_analyze
tools.title: Check whether a 3D model can be printed
tools.description: Measure a 3D model for real-world manufacturing: whether it is a closed solid, how many separate bodies it contains, how many holes it has, its thinnest wall, its exact volume, and a 0-100 printability score with named reasons. Also returns, per material, the smallest height the model can be printed at and still hold its detail. Free, keyless, and read-only: nothing is ordered. Pass a three.ws creation_id or any public glb_url. Use this before print_quote to check whether a model can be printed at all and how small it can go in each material.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before print_quote to check whether a model can be printed at all and how small it can go in each material.

glb_url.description: Public https URL of a .glb file, instead of a creation id.

tools.name: print_quote
tools.title: Price a real 3D print and get a signed quote
tools.description: Price a physical print of a 3D model: an itemized quote in USDC (build setup, material with the exact volume it was computed from, finish, quantity break, shipping) plus a signed quote token valid for 24 hours. Materials, size limits and lead times come from GET /api/print/catalog. This tool does NOT place an order and moves no money: settle the token at POST /api/x402/print-order when you have a shipping address. Free and keyless. Use this after print_analyze says the model is printable, when the user wants to know what a physical copy would cost.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after print_analyze says the model is printable, when the user wants to know what a physical copy would cost.

glb_url.description: Public https URL of a .glb file, instead of a creation id.

material_id.description: Material id from the catalog, e.g. resin-standard. Omit to list what fits.

finish_id.description: Optional finish id from that material.

quantity.description: How many. Price breaks at 5 and 20.

hollow.description: Hollow the solid where it is geometrically safe. Lowers the price.

note.description: Optional note about the intended object. Read by the fabrication safety gate.

tools.name: list_animations
tools.title: List animation presets
tools.description: List the curated, retargetable animation presets in the three.ws library - name, label, category, and whether the clip loops. Use this to discover valid `animation` values for apply_animation.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to discover valid `animation` values for apply_animation.

tools.name: animation_signature
tools.title: Measure what an animation clip actually does
tools.description: The measured motion signature of a baked clip: energy, tempo, which body region leads, loop-seam cleanliness, root travel, and whether it survives as an upper-body overlay. Pass `slot` to also get a fit verdict ("ok" or "warn" with the reason) for playing this clip in that runtime slot (idle, wave, fidget and the rest). Use it to pick clips by what they do rather than by name.
tools.whenToUse: Use it to pick clips by what they do rather than by name.

slot.description: Optional runtime slot to check the clip against (e.g. "idle", "fidget", "wave").

tools.name: find_similar_animations
tools.title: Find clips with similar measured motion
tools.description: Rank the library's clips by measured-motion distance from a reference clip (regional shares, energy, tempo, travel). Use it for "more like this": alternatives when a clip does not fit a slot, or variety without changing the mood.
tools.whenToUse: Use it for "more like this": alternatives when a clip does not fit a slot, or variety without changing the mood.

tools.name: apply_animation
tools.title: Apply an animation preset to a rigged model
tools.description: Retarget a curated animation preset onto a caller-supplied rigged humanoid GLB. Returns the retargeted three.js AnimationClip JSON (keyed to the rig's actual bone names, hip translation rescaled to its proportions) plus a retarget report; load it alongside the model and play. Set format="glb" to also bake an animated GLB server-side (best-effort: textured rigs may exceed the headless bake budget and fall back to clip JSON; the /pose gallery is the guaranteed GLB export). SSRF-hardened: only public https model URLs are fetched. Use this to put a ready-made motion from list_animations on your own rigged model; for a motion the library does not have, call text_to_animation.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to put a ready-made motion from list_animations on your own rigged model; for a motion the library does not have, call text_to_animation.

model_url.description: Public https URL of a rigged humanoid .glb to animate.

format.description: clip = retargeted AnimationClip JSON (reliable); glb = also attempt a baked animated GLB (base64, best-effort).

speed.description: Playback-speed multiplier baked into the result (1.8 turns a walk into a run).

tools.name: text_to_animation
tools.title: Generate an animation from a text prompt and retarget it onto a model
tools.description: Generate a brand-new motion from a natural-language prompt (e.g. "waving confidently", "a slow tai-chi sweep") with a motion-diffusion model, then retarget it onto a caller-supplied rigged humanoid GLB, using the same retarget engine as apply_animation. Returns the retargeted three.js AnimationClip JSON (or a baked animated GLB) plus a report. Unlike preset libraries, the motion does not pre-exist: it is synthesized for the prompt. Requires the text2motion worker configured on the deployment. Use this when no preset in list_animations fits the motion you want; when one does, apply_animation is faster and repeatable.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when no preset in list_animations fits the motion you want; when one does, apply_animation is faster and repeatable.

prompt.description: Describe the motion to generate (e.g. "a celebratory jump", "waving hello").

model_url.description: Public https URL of a rigged humanoid .glb to animate.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the generated motion in seconds.

format.description: clip = retargeted AnimationClip JSON (reliable); glb = also attempt a baked animated GLB.

speed.description: Playback-speed multiplier baked into the result.

tools.name: list_sign_vocabulary
tools.title: List the ASL vocabulary
tools.description: List every word three.ws avatars have a real American Sign Language sign for, with a plain description of the handshape, place on the body, and movement each one performs. Words outside this list are fingerspelled letter by letter instead. Use it to know in advance what a phrase will sign versus spell.
tools.whenToUse: Use it to know in advance what a phrase will sign versus spell.

search.description: Optional substring filter over the words and their descriptions.

tools.name: sign_text
tools.title: Sign text in ASL
tools.description: Compile English text into one continuous American Sign Language performance for a 3D avatar. Words with a real sign are signed; everything else is fingerspelled, in the same clip. Returns the performed timeline (every word, whether it signed or spelled, the seconds it occupies, and where each spelled letter lands) plus a link that plays it on a live avatar. Set include_clip to also get the three.js AnimationClip document, keyed to the canonical humanoid skeleton, to retarget onto any rigged avatar and play. Use this to make an avatar sign a phrase; to check beforehand which words will be signed rather than spelled, call list_sign_vocabulary.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to make an avatar sign a phrase; to check beforehand which words will be signed rather than spelled, call list_sign_vocabulary.

text.description: The text to sign. Letters, digits and spaces are performed; punctuation is dropped.

hand.description: Dominant signing hand. The whole sign mirrors, not just the hand.

speed.description: Playback rate, 0.25-1.5. Below 1 is a signer taking longer over the same signs.

max_seconds.description: Cap the utterance length; longer text truncates at a word boundary and is flagged.

include_clip.description: Include the full animation clip document. It is large (tens of thousands of numbers); leave it off and fetch clip_url when you need the bytes.

tools.name: solana_agent_reputation
tools.title: Get Solana agent reputation
tools.description: Computed reputation summary for a Solana-registered three.ws agent. Returns total/verified feedback counts, score averages (raw + verified-only), validation pass/fail, task acceptance, and dispute counts. Verified score only includes feedback whose task was acknowledged on-chain by the agent owner. Priced at $0.001 USDC/call via x402 (pay-per-call; an OAuth bearer token bypasses payment). Use this for a quick trust read on a Solana agent; for the individual records behind it call solana_agent_attestations, and for identity plus reputation in one call use solana_agent_passport.
tools.whenToUse: Use this for a quick trust read on a Solana agent; for the individual records behind it call solana_agent_attestations, and for identity plus reputation in one call use solana_agent_passport.

asset.description: Metaplex Core asset pubkey (the agent ID)

tools.name: solana_agent_attestations
tools.title: List Solana agent attestations
tools.description: List recent on-chain attestations about a Solana-registered agent (feedback, validation, task offers, acceptances, disputes). Backed by the three.ws indexer for sub-100ms reads. Each row includes verified/disputed/revoked flags. Public; no auth required. Use this to audit the individual feedback, validation, and dispute records behind a Solana agent reputation score; for the computed summary call solana_agent_reputation.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to audit the individual feedback, validation, and dispute records behind a Solana agent reputation score; for the computed summary call solana_agent_reputation.

tools.name: solana_agent_passport
tools.title: Get Solana agent passport
tools.description: Full discovery card for a Solana agent: identity (Metaplex Core asset), owner wallet, reputation summary, latest validation result, and attestation schema endpoint. Equivalent to an ERC-8004 passport. Use this when one tool call should answer "who is this agent and can I trust them?".
tools.whenToUse: Use this when one tool call should answer "who is this agent and can I trust them?".

tools.name: pumpfun_recent_claims
tools.title: Recent pump.fun claims
tools.description: Fetch the most recent pump.fun GitHub social-fee claim events with full enrichment: GitHub profile, X/Twitter follower data, influencer tier, first-time-claim flag, fake-claim detection, and AI summary. Use to answer 'what's happening on pump.fun right now?'.
tools.whenToUse: Use to answer 'what's happening on pump.fun right now?'.

tools.name: pumpfun_token_intel
tools.title: Pump.fun token intel
tools.description: Full intel on a pump.fun token: graduation status, bonding-curve progress, creator profile, top holders, volume, bundle detection, and trust signals. Use this before buying or discussing one pump.fun token; to vet the wallet that launched it call pumpfun_creator_intel.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before buying or discussing one pump.fun token; to vet the wallet that launched it call pumpfun_creator_intel.

mint.description: SPL mint pubkey (base58).

tools.name: pumpfun_creator_intel
tools.title: Pump.fun creator intel
tools.description: Reputation profile for a pump.fun creator wallet: prior launches, graduation rate, claim activity, and behavioural trust signals. Use this to judge whether a launcher has a track record of real launches before trusting a new coin from that wallet.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to judge whether a launcher has a track record of real launches before trusting a new coin from that wallet.

tools.name: pumpfun_recent_graduations
tools.title: Recent pump.fun graduations
tools.description: Tokens that recently graduated from the bonding curve to PumpAMM, with creator + holder analysis. Use this to see which pump.fun coins just left the bonding curve; for a deep read on one of them call pumpfun_token_intel.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to see which pump.fun coins just left the bonding curve; for a deep read on one of them call pumpfun_token_intel.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.title: Create an agent
tools.description: Create a new three.ws agent on your account: a named identity with a persona, a brain model, a custodial Solana wallet and a public page. Returns the agent id, its Solana address and its page URL. Read three://models (or read_resource uri "three://models") for the model ids. Creating an agent moves no funds; fund the wallet separately. Use this when the user wants a new agent; call list_my_agents first if they may already have one that fits.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the user wants a new agent; call list_my_agents first if they may already have one that fits.

name.description: Display name.

persona.description: Who the agent is and how it speaks. Becomes its system persona.

model.description: Brain model id from three://models agent_models (for example claude-sonnet-5). Omit for the free platform default.

avatar_id.description: An avatar you own to use as the body.

tools.name: call_agent
tools.title: Call agent
tools.description: Send a message to another three.ws agent and get its response. Use this to delegate specialized tasks.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to delegate specialized tasks.

agent_id.description: The agent's ID

tools.name: register_agent
tools.title: Register an agent on-chain
tools.description: Mint one of your agents' on-chain digital identity. On Solana (chain:solana) this enrols the agent in the Metaplex Agent Registry server-custodially - three.ws signs and pays, your wallet never has to - and returns the Agent Identity PDA, registration URI, and explorer link. On Base (chain:base) ERC-8004 registration needs your browser wallet to sign, so this returns a prepared registration_json plus a continue_url to finish in the browser. Idempotent: an already-registered agent is returned as-is unless force:true. Requires a signed-in three.ws account. Use this after create_agent when the agent needs a verifiable on-chain identity.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after create_agent when the agent needs a verifiable on-chain identity.

agent_id.description: Your agent identity id (uuid).

chain.description: Which chain to register on. solana = headless; base = ERC-8004 (needs your wallet).

network.description: Solana cluster (chain:solana only). Defaults to where the agent already lives, else the configured collection network.

force.description: Re-run registration even if the agent is already registered (never double-mints).

tools.name: attach_avatar_to_agent
tools.title: Give an agent a body
tools.description: Attach a generated/rigged avatar (from forge_avatar, mesh_forge + rig_mesh, or any avatar you own) to one of your registered agent identities - giving the agent a persistent visual body tied to its account identity. This is the bridge between generation and identity: generate a rigged GLB, save it as an avatar (list_my_avatars / the Forge 'Save' action), then call this tool to make it the agent's body. The same agent_id always shows the same body afterwards (get_avatar / render_avatar / get_embed_code all resolve it). Chain register_agent next to mint the on-chain identity (ERC-8004 on Base, or a Metaplex Agent Registry PDA on Solana) and anchor_provenance to credential the GLB itself - together the agent has a body, an on-chain identity, and a verifiable authenticity record. Requires a signed-in three.ws account; both the agent and the avatar must belong to the caller. Use this after saving a rigged avatar, to make it the permanent body of one of your agents.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after saving a rigged avatar, to make it the permanent body of one of your agents.

agent_id.description: Your agent identity id (uuid).

avatar_id.description: The avatar to attach (uuid) - one of your own avatars (see list_my_avatars).

tools.name: identity_check
tools.title: Screen an agent identity for impersonation
tools.description: Screen an agent identity (an existing agent_id, or a proposed name + description) for impersonation and policy violations before it goes public. Uses IBM Granite embeddings to find look-alike agents a name match would miss, and Granite Guardian to screen the identity text. Returns a clear | review | block verdict with the nearest neighbours and human-readable reasons. Use this before creating or publishing an agent to catch a name or description that copies an existing one.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before creating or publishing an agent to catch a name or description that copies an existing one.

agent_id.description: Screen one of your existing agents by id.

name.description: Proposed agent name (use with description instead of agent_id).

persona_tone_tags.description: Optional persona/tone tags to include in the embedded identity.

tools.name: list_my_agents
tools.title: List my agents
tools.description: List the agents on your account, newest first: id, name, description, brain model, public Solana address, whether the page is published and the page URL. Use this first to get the agent ids that recall, list_custom_skills, attach_avatar_to_agent and call_agent need. Reads only; no funds move.
tools.whenToUse: Use this first to get the agent ids that recall, list_custom_skills, attach_avatar_to_agent and call_agent need.

tools.name: list_available_skills
tools.title: Browse community skills
tools.description: Search the public three.ws community skills registry: prompt-only skills (a SKILL.md of instructions) anyone can contribute by pull request and import onto an agent in one call. Filter by free text, tag, or author. Each result carries slug, name, description, author, tags, version and an estimated token size. Import one with import_community_skill. Use this to find a ready-made skill before writing one from scratch with create_custom_skill.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find a ready-made skill before writing one from scratch with create_custom_skill.

include_content.description: Also return each SKILL.md body (larger response).

tools.name: import_community_skill
tools.title: Import a community skill onto an agent
tools.description: Install a community registry skill (see list_available_skills) on one of your agents as an editable prompt-only custom skill. From the next message on, the agent follows the skill in every chat, within its per-agent token budget. Returns the new skill and the updated budget. Installing the same skill twice returns already_installed with the existing skill_id. Use this after list_available_skills when a registry skill fits; to write your own instead call create_custom_skill.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after list_available_skills when a registry skill fits; to write your own instead call create_custom_skill.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_agents or GET /api/agents lists them.

tools.name: list_custom_skills
tools.title: List an agent's custom skills
tools.description: List every prompt-only custom skill on one of your agents in install order, with each skill's token size, whether it is injected into the prompt right now (skip_reason: disabled | over_budget), and the agent's budget (cap 6000 tokens). Imported skills report whether the registry has a newer revision. Use this to see what an agent already follows, and whether it all fits the budget, before adding or editing a skill.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to see what an agent already follows, and whether it all fits the budget, before adding or editing a skill.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_agents or GET /api/agents lists them.

tools.name: get_custom_skill
tools.title: Get one custom skill
tools.description: Read one custom skill on your agent, full text included, plus where it lands in the agent's token budget. Call this before delete_custom_skill and show the user the skill, or before update_custom_skill to see the text you are changing.
tools.whenToUse: Call this before delete_custom_skill and show the user the skill, or before update_custom_skill to see the text you are changing.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_agents or GET /api/agents lists them.

skill_id.description: The custom skill id (uuid) from list_custom_skills.

tools.name: create_custom_skill
tools.title: Write a custom skill for an agent
tools.description: Write a new prompt-only skill on one of your agents: markdown instructions the agent follows whenever a message falls in the skill's domain. Up to 24000 characters. Skills are injected oldest first inside a 6000-token budget per agent; the response says whether this one fits. Use this when no registry skill fits (check list_available_skills) and the agent needs standing instructions of your own.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when no registry skill fits (check list_available_skills) and the agent needs standing instructions of your own.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_agents or GET /api/agents lists them.

slug.description: Optional; derived from name when omitted.

tools.name: update_custom_skill
tools.title: Edit or toggle a custom skill
tools.description: Edit a custom skill on your agent: rename it, rewrite its instructions, retag it, enable or disable it (a disabled skill stays saved but is not injected), or pass resync:true to pull the latest registry revision of an imported skill (overwrites local edits). Use this to change a skill in place, including switching it off without deleting it.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to change a skill in place, including switching it off without deleting it.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_agents or GET /api/agents lists them.

skill_id.description: The custom skill id (uuid) from list_custom_skills.

tools.name: delete_custom_skill
tools.title: Delete a custom skill
tools.description: Permanently delete a custom skill from your agent. Irreversible: a hand-written skill cannot be recovered. Use this when the user explicitly wants the skill gone for good. First call get_custom_skill, show the user the skill, and wait for a clear yes; then call this with confirm_delete: true. To stop a skill without losing it, use update_custom_skill with enabled:false instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the user explicitly wants the skill gone for good.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_agents or GET /api/agents lists them.

skill_id.description: The custom skill id (uuid) from list_custom_skills.

confirm_delete.description: Must be true. Set only after the user confirmed.

tools.name: browse_external_skills
tools.title: Browse external skill registries
tools.description: Browse SKILL.md skills from public registries: the three.ws community repository, the public Anthropic agent skills repository, skills published on three.ws, and any GitHub repository or manifest the owner added. Each skill carries its registry, pinned commit or sha256, licence, author, category (defi, intelligence, social, infrastructure, security, data) and how many agents installed it. Skills whose licence does not permit reuse are listed under `excluded` with the reason, never offered. Reads only. To install one, call scan_external_skill with its `key`. Use this when the owner wants a ready-made skill for an agent instead of writing one.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the owner wants a ready-made skill for an agent instead of writing one.

registry.description: Limit to one registry key (from a previous result), e.g. "github:nirholas/three.ws/community-skills/skills" or "published".

q.description: Free text matched against name, description, tags and slug.

limit.description: Most skills to return, most installed first.

tools.name: scan_external_skill
tools.title: Scan an external skill for install
tools.description: Fetch one external skill at its pinned revision and scan it before install: licence, size and token budget, hidden or overriding instructions, secret harvesting, exfiltration links, hardcoded payout addresses, and whether it asks to spend, sign or send messages (which puts it under the spend gate). Opens an import request that holds the exact scanned bytes for 24 hours; nothing is installed. Show the owner the provenance, verdict, findings and capabilities, and only after they say yes call install_external_skill with the request_id. A `refused` verdict can never be installed. Call this first for any skill picked from browse_external_skills; nothing can be installed without its request_id.
tools.whenToUse: Call this first for any skill picked from browse_external_skills; nothing can be installed without its request_id.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_my_agents lists them.

skill.description: The skill `key` from browse_external_skills (or its slug within the registry).

tools.name: install_external_skill
tools.title: Install a scanned external skill
tools.description: Install (or, for an update request, apply) exactly the bytes a scan_external_skill or external_skill_update_diff request holds, as a prompt-only skill on the agent. Only call this after the owner saw that scan and explicitly approved; pass owner_approved: true. A skill that asks to spend, sign or message also needs acknowledge_gated: true, and runs under the spend gate: any transfer the agent proposes while it is active is held unless the owner's own message asked for that amount and recipient. To decline instead, pass decision: "refuse". Call this once the owner has approved the scanned request, within its 24 hours.
tools.whenToUse: Call this once the owner has approved the scanned request, within its 24 hours.

request_id.description: The request_id from scan_external_skill or external_skill_update_diff.

owner_approved.description: Must be true: the owner saw the scan and said yes.

acknowledge_gated.description: Required true for a gated skill, after telling the owner it will run under the spend gate.

decision.description: approve installs; refuse closes the request.

tools.name: external_skill_update_diff
tools.title: Check an imported skill for upstream changes
tools.description: Compare an installed external skill with its registry's current revision. Installed imports are pinned, so upstream changes never apply on their own. If upstream changed, returns the unified diff, line stats, whether the owner edited their copy, and a freshly scanned update request; show the owner the diff and scan, and apply it with install_external_skill only after they approve. Unchanged returns changed: false. Use this when the owner asks whether an imported skill has upstream updates.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the owner asks whether an imported skill has upstream updates.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_my_agents lists them.

open_request.description: false previews the diff without opening an update request.

tools.name: skill_fork
tools.title: Fork a skill
tools.description: Copy a skill onto one of your agents as your own editable custom skill: any skill on any agent you own (imported, community or hand-written), or a skill published on three.ws by slug. The fork records where it came from and keeps the upstream licence; a fork of a gated skill stays gated. Edit it with update_custom_skill, then share it with skill_publish. Use this when the owner wants to change a skill they did not write, or keep their own copy of one.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the owner wants to change a skill they did not write, or keep their own copy of one.

agent_id.description: The agent that receives the fork.

skill_id.description: A skill id on any agent you own. Give this or published_slug.

published_slug.description: A slug from the three.ws published registry. Give this or skill_id.

name.description: Name for the fork; defaults to the original name.

tools.name: skill_publish
tools.title: Publish a skill to the three.ws registry
tools.description: Publish one of your own skills (hand-written, or a fork you changed) to the public three.ws skill registry, where anyone can browse and import it with you credited as author. The skill is scanned first and a refused scan cannot be published; an unchanged import is someone else's work and must be forked and changed first; a fork of copyleft work keeps that licence. Publishing again replaces the public copy. Ask the owner first, then pass confirm_publish: true. Use this when the owner wants to share a skill they wrote or changed with everyone on three.ws.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the owner wants to share a skill they wrote or changed with everyone on three.ws.

agent_id.description: Your agent id (uuid). list_my_agents lists them.

license.description: The licence to publish under (SPDX id).

confirm_publish.description: Must be true: the owner agreed to make this skill public.

tools.name: remember
tools.title: Remember
tools.description: Store a long-term memory for one of your agents. Use for durable facts: who the user is (type=user), guidance/corrections (feedback), ongoing work (project), or external pointers (reference). Returns the stored memory.
tools.whenToUse: Use for durable facts: who the user is (type=user), guidance/corrections (feedback), ongoing work (project), or external pointers (reference).

context.description: Optional freeform metadata about where this memory came from.

expires_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 expiry; the memory is excluded from recall after this time.

tools.name: recall
tools.title: Recall
tools.description: Retrieve the most relevant memories for a query from one of your agents. Ranks by relevance to the query blended with salience and recency, excluding expired memories. Returns an ordered list. Use this before answering when an agent should draw on what it already knows about the user or the work; to save a new fact call remember.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before answering when an agent should draw on what it already knows about the user or the work; to save a new fact call remember.

tools.name: forget
tools.title: Forget
tools.description: Delete a memory you own by its id. Use this when a stored memory is wrong or outdated, or the user asks the agent to forget it; find the id with recall.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when a stored memory is wrong or outdated, or the user asks the agent to forget it; find the id with recall.

tools.name: oracle_top_plays
tools.title: Oracle top conviction plays
tools.description: Get the current top pump.fun launches ranked by Oracle conviction score. Each play includes a score (0-100), tier (prime/strong/lean/watch/avoid), four pillar scores (pedigree/structure/narrative/momentum), and an agent-ready recommendation with a suggested size_factor. Use this to decide which coins to buy before they move. Filter by min_score or category to narrow the signal.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to decide which coins to buy before they move.

limit.description: Number of plays to return (default 5, max 20).

tools.name: oracle_coin
tools.title: Oracle verdict for one coin
tools.description: Get Oracle's full conviction verdict for a specific pump.fun coin by mint address. Returns the fused 0-100 conviction score, tier (prime/strong/lean/watch/avoid), all four pillar scores (pedigree = who's behind it, structure = how it's built, narrative = cultural fit, momentum = early trading signal), active badges (e.g. smart_money_early, narrative_match), and a machine-readable buy/watch/skip recommendation. If the coin isn't in the Oracle cache yet, it will be scored on-demand (may add ~1s latency). Use this when you already have a specific mint in mind; for the ranked board of current plays call oracle_top_plays.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you already have a specific mint in mind; for the ranked board of current plays call oracle_top_plays.

mint.description: SPL mint pubkey (base58) of the pump.fun coin.

tools.name: oracle_arm_watch
tools.title: Arm agent Oracle watch
tools.description: Arm your agent to automatically act on Oracle conviction signals. Once armed, the Oracle cron (every 2 min) will detect high-conviction launches that cross your floor and execute buys from your agent's custodial Solana wallet. Set mode='simulate' (default, safe) to log what it would have bought without spending. Set mode='live' to spend real SOL. The agent acts at most once per mint, per-trade SOL is capped, and you can disarm at any time by passing armed=false. Use this when the owner wants the agent to buy high-conviction Oracle picks on its own; check the setup and results afterwards with oracle_watch_status.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the owner wants the agent to buy high-conviction Oracle picks on its own; check the setup and results afterwards with oracle_watch_status.

agent_id.description: Your agent UUID (from /api/agents or the dashboard).

armed.description: true to arm, false to disarm.

mode.description: simulate = no real spend (safe default). live = real SOL from agent's wallet.

min_score.description: Conviction floor to act on (72 = strong+; 90 = prime only).

min_tier.description: Alternative to min_score: acts on this tier and above.

categories.description: Only act on coins in these narrative categories. Omit to act on all.

per_trade_sol.description: Max SOL per single trade (default 0.05). Ignored in simulate mode.

max_daily_sol.description: Daily SOL budget cap (default 0.5). The loop will not spend more in one day.

require_smart_money.description: Only act when at least one proven smart-money wallet is in early.

size_scaling.description: Scale position size with conviction (prime = full, strong = 75%, lean = 50%).

tools.name: oracle_watch_status
tools.title: Oracle watch status + track record
tools.description: Check your agent's current Oracle watch configuration and its realized track record: win rate, PnL, ROI, plus the 10 most recent actions with their outcomes. Use this to verify the agent is armed correctly and to review its performance before scaling up.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to verify the agent is armed correctly and to review its performance before scaling up.

agent_id.description: Your agent UUID.

tools.name: trader_leaderboard
tools.title: Top pump.fun traders
tools.description: Get the top pump.fun traders on three.ws ranked by composite TraderScore (win rate + P&L + ROI + drawdown). Each row includes score (0-100), verified badge, closed trade count, win rate, realized P&L in SOL and USD, ROI %, max drawdown, and a 'recommendation' field: 'copy' = strong candidate, 'watch' = emerging, 'skip' = unproven. Use this to find leaders worth copying, then call trader_profile for full details before you copy one. Sort by 'score' (default), 'pnl', 'winrate', or 'roi'. Window: '24h', '7d', '30d' (default), or 'all'.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find leaders worth copying, then call trader_profile for full details before you copy one.

verified_only.description: Only return verified traders (12+ closed trades, 5+ unique coins, <40% churn).

tools.name: trader_profile
tools.title: Full track record for one agent
tools.description: Get the full, verifiable track record for a specific pump.fun agent trader. Returns the composite TraderScore, all headline metrics (win rate, realized P&L, ROI, profit factor, max drawdown, average hold time), up to 10 recent closed trades with their on-chain Solscan links, and any open positions. Every number is traceable to its on-chain buy/sell transaction. Use this to vet an agent before calling copy_subscribe.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to vet an agent before calling copy_subscribe.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from trader_leaderboard rows or /api/agents).

tools.name: trade_receipt
tools.title: Why an agent took one trade
tools.description: Get the decision receipt for one pump.fun trade by an agent: the entry trigger, the Oracle conviction score and pillars at entry with the base-rate reasons behind it, the trade firewall verdict and its checks (including the simulated buy/sell round-trip), the LLM judge's thesis when one ran, the Risk Officer review, paid x402 sentiment and rug-pull reads with their payment transaction, launch intel, and every journal leg with its on-chain signature. Evidence recorded after the exit is excluded because it could not have caused the trade; evidence seen while holding is tagged during_trade. Use this to understand what a leader actually trades on before copying it, passing a trade_id from trader_profile's recent_trades.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to understand what a leader actually trades on before copying it, passing a trade_id from trader_profile's recent_trades.

tools.name: sentiment_scout
tools.title: Sourced momentum candidates (Sentiment Scout)
tools.description: Surface pump.fun momentum candidates with evidence you can cite. Each candidate returns a 0-100 momentum_score (with the parts that add up to it), evidence lines of type volume_spike, fresh_buyers, smart_money, graduation_approach, social_mention (X posts quoting the coin's exact contract address, or pump.fun callouts), paid_signal (x402 market reads with their payment transaction) and news_match, and one caution line naming the main risk. Every evidence line carries source (a URL that returns the fact), at (when it was true) and, for social or paid claims, checked_against (the on-chain facts read in the same run). Sources that could not be read are listed in unavailable, never estimated. Pass mint to read one coin even if it would not make the board. Pass track_record=true to include how the coins the Scout flagged over the last 14 days actually did against the base rate. This tool never trades and is not advice; cite the evidence, not the score. Use this to find which pump.fun coins are gaining momentum right now and why; for a full conviction verdict on one coin call oracle_coin.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find which pump.fun coins are gaining momentum right now and why; for a full conviction verdict on one coin call oracle_coin.

mint.description: Optional pump.fun mint (base58). Omit for the board.

window_minutes.description: Minutes of launches to rank against.

track_record.description: Include the Scout's graded track record.

tools.name: copy_subscribe
tools.title: Subscribe to copy a trader
tools.description: Set up non-custodial copy-trading: mirror a leader agent's future pump.fun entries into your own wallet with your own sizing and risk caps. You supply your wallet address and the sizing rules; we never hold keys. The fan-out cron checks for new leader entries and generates sized intents you act on from /dashboard/copy. Provide leader_agent_id (from trader_leaderboard) and your Solana wallet address. Sizing rules: 'fixed' = exact SOL per trade, 'multiplier' = N× leader size, 'pct_balance' = % of your balance. Always set a per_trade_cap_sol and daily_budget_sol to limit exposure. Calling this again for the same leader and network updates that subscription in place: sizing, caps and perf_fee_bps are replaced by what you send, so anything you omit falls back to its default, while the Oracle-score floor, market-cap band and Telegram route are kept as they were. Clear those three from /dashboard/copy. Use this after vetting a leader with trader_profile, when the user wants to mirror that leader's trades.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after vetting a leader with trader_profile, when the user wants to mirror that leader's trades.

leader_agent_id.description: The agent UUID to copy (from trader_leaderboard).

copier_wallet.description: Your Solana wallet address (base58) that will receive the copy intents.

sizing_rule.description: How to size your copies relative to the leader.

pct_balance.description: Percent of your balance per trade (sizing_rule=pct_balance).

per_trade_cap_sol.description: Hard cap: no single copy trade may exceed this SOL amount.

daily_budget_sol.description: Hard daily spend ceiling across all copy trades.

min_order_sol.description: Skip copies that would be smaller than this SOL amount.

min_oracle_score.description: Only copy leader entries where Oracle conviction is at least this score.

mcap_floor_usd.description: Skip coins below this USD market cap at entry.

mcap_ceiling_usd.description: Skip coins above this USD market cap at entry (avoid already-pumped).

telegram_chat_id.description: Telegram chat ID for copy-execution alerts (optional).

perf_fee_bps.description: Performance fee in bps paid to the leader on wins (default 10%).

tools.name: copy_status
tools.title: My copy subscriptions
tools.description: List all your active copy-trading subscriptions, with sizing config, execution counts (pending/acted), and the leader's name and profile. Use this to check that copy-trading is set up correctly and to see which subscriptions are generating intents.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to check that copy-trading is set up correctly and to see which subscriptions are generating intents.

tools.name: mint_3d_asset
tools.title: Mint a 3D asset as a Solana NFT
tools.description: Mint a generated or owned GLB as a Metaplex Core NFT on Solana whose media is a LIVE, interactive 3D viewer (the rigged glTF model under animation_url, not a static image). Bakes provenance (creator, prompt, generation model, parent lineage, timestamp) into the metadata AND appends a signed, independently-verifiable record to the agent_actions provenance ledger; enforces capped creator royalties on secondary sales. Supply an owned avatar_id or a glb_url, and a recipient (owner_wallet, or your OAuth-linked Solana wallet). Devnet by default; pass network="mainnet" for a real mainnet mint. Idempotent (a repeat call for the same asset returns the same mint). Royalty is capped at 10%. Naming parent_mint (a remix/derivative on mainnet) routes the parent creator's royalty slice out of THIS mint's fee as a real on-chain USDC transfer. Returns the mint address, explorer + viewer links, royalty terms, the provenance ledger reference, and (for a remix) the royalty settlement. Priced per call via x402 (USDC); an OAuth bearer token bypasses payment within a small per-account mint budget (5 mainnet mints a day). Use this when the user wants a model to exist as an ownable, tradable on-chain asset; to read one back call get_3d_asset_onchain.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the user wants a model to exist as an ownable, tradable on-chain asset; to read one back call get_3d_asset_onchain.

avatar_id.description: An owned avatar to tokenize (its GLB becomes the NFT media).

glb_url.description: Or a GLB URL to tokenize (absolute http(s)).

owner_wallet.description: Recipient Solana wallet (base58). Defaults to your OAuth-linked wallet when omitted.

name.description: Display name for the NFT.

network.description: Cluster to mint on. Devnet by default; mainnet is a real mint.

seller_fee_basis_points.description: Enforced secondary-sale royalty in basis points. Clamped to the 10% hard cap.

royalty_recipient.description: Wallet the royalty routes to (base58). Defaults to the owner.

parent_mint.description: Lineage: the asset this was remixed from (baked into provenance).

prompt.description: Generation prompt (provenance).

idempotency_key.description: Override the derived idempotency key to force-dedupe a specific request.

tools.name: get_3d_asset_onchain
tools.title: Resolve a 3D NFT to its live asset + provenance
tools.description: Resolve a Solana mint address to its live 3D asset: current holder, the interactive viewer link + GLB (confirmed live), baked provenance (creator, prompt, model, lineage, timestamp), and the enforced on-chain royalty terms. Works on any Metaplex Core mint. Assets minted through three.ws also return their platform launch record. Read-only, public. Use this to check who holds a 3D NFT and what its provenance and royalty terms are.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to check who holds a 3D NFT and what its provenance and royalty terms are.

mint.description: The Metaplex Core asset (mint) pubkey, base58.

network.description: Cluster to read (ignored if the mint is in our launch records).

tools.name: crypto_data
tools.title: Crypto Data API
tools.description:
Call any endpoint in the three.ws free crypto data API (the same aggregator behind GET /api/v1/x/*): DEX pairs, CoinGecko/DefiLlama market data, Jupiter Solana prices and swap quotes, and direct Solana RPC reads. Endpoints marked free run within a per-IP quota, no wallet needed; an endpoint with no free tier (or an exhausted quota) returns a payment-required error naming the exact REST URL and USDC price to pay via x402. Use this for raw data from one named provider endpoint; for a merged one-call view of a Solana token call token_snapshot.

Live provider/endpoint pairs on this deployment:
coingecko/price: Spot price for one or more coins in any fiat/crypto.
coingecko/markets: Ranked market data (price, market cap, volume, change) per coin.
coingecko/coin: Full market snapshot for one coin - price, ATH/ATL, supply, multi-window change, truncated description.
coingecko/trending: Top trending searched coins and hot categories right now.
coingecko/token-price: Spot price for one or more token contract addresses on a given chain (default Solana).
coingecko/global: Global crypto market snapshot - total market cap/volume, BTC/ETH dominance, active coin count.
coingecko/ohlc: OHLC candles for one coin over 1/7/14/30 days.
defillama/protocols: All DeFi protocols with current TVL, ranked.
defillama/tvl: Current total value locked (USD) for a single protocol.
defillama/chains: Every chain DefiLlama tracks, with current TVL, ranked.
defillama/protocol: One protocol: category, per-chain current TVL, and the last 30 points of its total TVL series.
defillama/chain-tvl: Last 90 days of historical total TVL for one chain.
llama-prices/current: Current price for one or more chain:address tokens (DefiLlama coin-price oracle - covers tokens CoinGecko/Jupiter don't index).
llama-stablecoins/list: Every tracked stablecoin - peg type, price, circulating supply - ranked by circulating USD.
jupiter/price: Live USD price for one or more Solana tokens by mint (Jupiter keyless tier).
jupiter/quote: Executable swap quote (true routed price) between two Solana mints (Jupiter keyless tier).
jupiter/token-search: Search Solana tokens by name/symbol/mint → address, metadata, tags, 24h volume (Jupiter keyless tier).
openai/chat: Chat completions against any OpenAI-compatible model (BYOK supported).
grok/chat: Chat completions against xAI Grok models (grok-4.7, grok-4.3, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, grok-build-0.1; BYOK supported).
dexscreener/token: Live DEX pairs (price, liquidity, volume, txns) for one or more token addresses, deepest liquidity first.
dexscreener/search: Search DEX pairs by token name, symbol, or address, deepest liquidity first.
dexscreener/pair: Live pair data for one DexScreener chainId + on-chain pair address.
dexscreener/profiles: Latest DexScreener token profiles - freshly listed projects with descriptions and social links.
dexscreener/boosts: Latest DexScreener boosted tokens - paid promotion signal, not an endorsement or ranking by quality.
solana/balance: Native SOL balance of any wallet address.
solana/token-holdings: SPL token holdings of a wallet (mint, amount, decimals), zero balances filtered, largest first.
solana/token-supply: Total circulating supply of an SPL token mint.
solana/largest-holders: Top 20 holder token-accounts of an SPL token mint by balance.
solana/transaction: Confirmed transaction detail by signature - fee, error, signers, log lines, and SPL token balance deltas.
solana/account: Account info for any address - owning program, lamports, executable flag, parsed data type.
solana/priority-fees: Recent prioritization fee landscape (p50/p75/p95/max micro-lamports) over the last ~150 slots.
tools.whenToUse: Use this for raw data from one named provider endpoint; for a merged one-call view of a Solana token call token_snapshot.

endpoint.description: Endpoint id under that provider, e.g. "price", "token", "quote".

params.description: Endpoint-specific query params. See the endpoint summary in the tool description for required fields.

tools.name: token_snapshot
tools.title: Crypto token snapshot
tools.description: One-call snapshot for a Solana token mint, fanning out to whichever free crypto-data providers are registered on this deployment (DexScreener pairs, Jupiter price, Solana RPC supply) and merging what answers. Degrades gracefully around any provider that is absent, unconfigured, or fails, never throwing on a partial result. Example mint: the $THREE CA "FeMbDoX7R1Psc4GEcvJdsbNbZA3bfztcyDCatJVJpump". For pump.fun-specific bonding-curve / launch data use the pump_snapshot tool instead. Use this for a quick general market read on one Solana token (price, liquidity, supply) without choosing providers yourself.
tools.whenToUse: Use this for a quick general market read on one Solana token (price, liquidity, supply) without choosing providers yourself.

mint.description: Base58 Solana token mint address.

tools.name: generate_garment
tools.title: Generate a wearable garment from a text prompt
tools.description: Turn a text prompt (e.g. "a red varsity jacket") into a rigged, wearable garment published to the three.ws wardrobe catalog. The pipeline generates a reference image, sculpts a PBR mesh on the GPU fleet, skins it to the canonical humanoid skeleton, and validates it (including the 60% bind-coverage gate) before publishing garment.glb + manifest.json + thumbnail. Runs asynchronously for about 7 minutes; poll with garment_status. The finished piece appears in the public catalog automatically and attaches to any humanoid avatar. Use this when nothing in list_garment_catalog fits and the user wants a new wearable item made.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when nothing in list_garment_catalog fits and the user wants a new wearable item made.

prompt.description: Describe the garment (fabric, color, style).

tools.name: garment_status
tools.title: Check a garment generation job
tools.description: Poll a generate_garment job. While running, reports the pipeline stage. When done, returns the published glb_url, manifest_url, thumbnail, measured bind coverage, and the occluded body regions. At that point the garment is already live in the wardrobe catalog. Use this after generate_garment to follow the job until it finishes.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after generate_garment to follow the job until it finishes.

tools.name: list_garment_catalog
tools.title: List the wardrobe garment catalog
tools.description: Fetch the public three.ws wardrobe catalog: every published garment manifest (id, slot, name, GLB url, thumbnail, occluded regions). Any entry attaches to any humanoid avatar via the additive wardrobe. Use this to pick an existing garment before generating a new one with generate_garment.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to pick an existing garment before generating a new one with generate_garment.

slot.description: Optional: only garments for this slot.

tools.name: list_feedback
tools.title: List feedback
tools.description: What visitors reported is broken, grouped into one row per distinct problem, loudest first. Each row carries the severity, the subsystem, how many people hit it, and whether a recorded session exists that can be compiled into a failing test with get_feedback_repro. Admin only. Use this to decide which visitor-reported bug to fix next.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to decide which visitor-reported bug to fix next.

replayable_only.description: Only clusters that carry a recorded session, which are the ones an agent can verify a fix against.

tools.name: get_feedback_repro
tools.title: Compile a feedback report into a failing test
tools.description: Compile one feedback report into a runnable Playwright spec from the session the visitor actually recorded. The spec asserts the reported failure is GONE, so it is red while the bug exists and green once it is fixed: Use it to reproduce the bug before changing anything, and to prove the change worked. Returns the spec source, the narrated steps, and a replay-confidence score. Admin only, read-only.
tools.whenToUse: Use it to reproduce the bug before changing anything, and to prove the change worked.

base_url.description: Origin the replay runs against. Defaults to production; pass a local dev origin to run it against a working copy.

tools.name: home_status
tools.title: Home status
tools.description: Read the current state of a connected home: its rooms, what is lit, the temperature, and whether it is locked up. Use this to answer "is the house locked?", "are the lights on downstairs?", or before proposing an action, so you act on what the house is rather than what you assume. Returns a per-room rollup and a stale flag when the live connection has dropped.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to answer "is the house locked?", "are the lights on downstairs?", or before proposing an action, so you act on what the house is rather than what you assume.

home_id.description: Which connected home. Omit when the account has exactly one.

room.description: Optional: narrow to one room by name.

tools.name: home_list_macros
tools.title: List home scenes and scripts
tools.description: List the scenes and scripts this house already has. Prefer running one of these over composing your own sequence of calls: the household's own "Bedtime" scene knows about the plant light and the fish tank, and you do not. Call this before home_activate so you propose something that exists.
tools.whenToUse: Call this before home_activate so you propose something that exists.

home_id.description: Which connected home. Omit when the account has exactly one.

tools.name: home_grants
tools.title: Standing home permissions
tools.description: List the entities this home has pre-approved, so a guarded action on one of them runs without asking. Call this before proposing something that would otherwise need a confirmation: if the entity is already granted, there is no prompt to warn the user about.
tools.whenToUse: Call this before proposing something that would otherwise need a confirmation: if the entity is already granted, there is no prompt to warn the user about.

home_id.description: Which connected home. Omit when the account has exactly one.

tools.name: home_activate
tools.title: Activate a home scene
tools.description: Match a phrase like "good night" or "I am home" to one of this house's own scenes or scripts, and run it. Returns the match and how confident it is. If the scene would unlock, open, or disarm something, this does NOT run it: it returns a pending confirmation that a person has to approve. Use this when the user asks for a household routine in plain words; if no scene or script fits, use home_call instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the user asks for a household routine in plain words; if no scene or script fits, use home_call instead.

home_id.description: Which connected home. Omit when the account has exactly one.

phrase.description: What the person said, e.g. "good night".

dry_run.description: Report the match without running it.

tools.name: home_call
tools.title: Call a home service
tools.description: Call a Home Assistant service, e.g. light.turn_on with {"entity_id": "light.kitchen"}. Use this when no scene fits. Locking up, closing, and arming run immediately. Unlocking, opening, and disarming do NOT: they return a pending confirmation that a person has to approve out of band, and there is no argument you can pass to skip that. Target with entity_id, device_id, area_id, or floor_id; every target is resolved to concrete entities before it runs.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when no scene fits.

home_id.description: Which connected home. Omit when the account has exactly one.

data.description: Service data, including the target (entity_id / device_id / area_id / floor_id) and any parameters.

tools.name: read_resource
tools.title: Read a three:// resource
tools.description: Read a live three.ws resource by URI: three://me (account, scopes, quota), three://agents and three://agents/<id> (your agents), three://agents/<id>/wallet (balances, limits, freeze state), .../usage, .../chat, .../runs, .../orders, .../dca, .../intents, .../earnings (public: creator fees, claims, service income), three://wallets, three://launches, three://marketplace, three://models and three://x402/services. Omit uri to list every resource you can read. Set format to markdown for a readable rendering. Use this to read account, agent, wallet, or catalog state that has no dedicated tool, or to see what is readable when unsure.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to read account, agent, wallet, or catalog state that has no dedicated tool, or to see what is readable when unsure.

uri.description: A three:// resource URI, for example three://me or three://agents/<agentId>/wallet. Omit to list every resource you can read here.

tools.name: agent_card_search_merchants
tools.title: Search card merchants
tools.description: Search merchants an agent can buy a gift card or prepaid card from (for example a game store, a marketplace, food delivery, or a prepaid Visa). Returns merchant names with the countries and categories they sell in. Pass sandbox: true to list the provider's free test products, which run the whole purchase flow without moving funds. Use this first when the owner wants to buy a gift or prepaid card, then pick a product with agent_card_search_gift_cards.
tools.whenToUse: Use this first when the owner wants to buy a gift or prepaid card, then pick a product with agent_card_search_gift_cards.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

q.description: Merchant or brand name to search for.

kind.description: Only gift cards or only prepaid cards.

tools.name: agent_card_search_gift_cards
tools.title: Search gift and prepaid card products
tools.description: Search card products with their denominations: fixed packages and/or an allowed range, currency, country and stock. Use this after agent_card_search_merchants to choose a product and an allowed amount, then pass both to agent_card_quote.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after agent_card_search_merchants to choose a product and an allowed amount, then pass both to agent_card_quote.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_quote
tools.title: Quote a card purchase
tools.description: Lock a price for one card: returns the total in USDC including fees, the Solana address it would be paid to, a quote_id valid for ten minutes, and a confirm table (recipient, amount, token, chain). Moves no funds. Use this before agent_card_create, and show the confirm table to the owner before buying.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before agent_card_create, and show the confirm table to the owner before buying.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

amount.description: Face value in the product currency; must be a package value or inside the range.

tools.name: agent_card_create
tools.title: Buy a card from the agent wallet
tools.description: Buy the card a quote describes, paying the quoted USDC from the agent wallet on Solana under the agent's spend limits and anomaly freeze. Requires a quote_id from agent_card_quote that is under ten minutes old and confirm_spend: true, which you may only send after the owner explicitly approved the quote's confirm table. Returns the card with its status and the payment signature. Use this after the owner said yes to the exact quote; follow the card afterwards with agent_card_status.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after the owner said yes to the exact quote; follow the card afterwards with agent_card_status.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

confirm_spend.description: Must be true, and only after the owner said yes to the quote.

tools.name: agent_card_list
tools.title: List agent cards
tools.description: List the agent's cards, newest first, with masked numbers, status and what each cost. In-flight cards are refreshed from the provider. Use this to find a card id or see what the agent has bought; for one card with its full audit trail call agent_card_get.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find a card id or see what the agent has bought; for one card with its full audit trail call agent_card_get.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_get
tools.title: Get one agent card
tools.description: One card with its audit trail (quotes, payment, status changes, reveals with who and when). Never includes the secret. Use this to answer who paid for, revealed, or changed a card and when; for the code or PIN itself go through agent_card_data and agent_card_reveal.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to answer who paid for, revealed, or changed a card and when; for the code or PIN itself go through agent_card_data and agent_card_reveal.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_status
tools.title: Refresh a card from the provider
tools.description: Ask the provider for the card's current status (processing, delivered, failed, refunded) and update the record. Use this when a card is still processing, or to confirm it was delivered before revealing it.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when a card is still processing, or to confirm it was delivered before revealing it.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_balance
tools.title: Card balance
tools.description: The card's remaining balance. When the provider does not report balances the answer is the face value of a delivered card, and says so. Use this before agent_card_withdraw, or when the owner asks how much is left on a card.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before agent_card_withdraw, or when the owner asks how much is left on a card.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_data
tools.title: Card data and reveal preview
tools.description: The masked card number, which secret fields exist (code, PIN, link) and redemption instructions, plus a single-use preview_id valid for five minutes. Call this before agent_card_reveal, which needs the preview_id it returns. Does not expose the secret.
tools.whenToUse: Call this before agent_card_reveal, which needs the preview_id it returns.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_reveal
tools.title: Reveal a card secret once
tools.description: Return the card number, PIN or redemption code. Requires the preview_id from agent_card_data and confirm_reveal: true after the owner agreed. The preview id works once; the stored encrypted copy is deleted by this call, and the reveal is logged with the actor and time. Treat the result as a secret: give it to the owner only, never post it anywhere. Use this when the owner asks for the code to redeem the card, and at no other time.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the owner asks for the code to redeem the card, and at no other time.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_cancel
tools.title: Cancel a card
tools.description: Cancel a card. Unpaid quotes can always be cancelled; whether a paid card can be depends on the provider, and the error says so when it cannot. Requires confirm_cancel: true. Use this when the owner no longer wants a quoted or pending card.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the owner no longer wants a quoted or pending card.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_withdraw
tools.title: Withdraw a prepaid balance to USDC
tools.description: Move a prepaid card balance back to the agent wallet as USDC, where the provider supports it. Check agent_card_balance first and pass confirm_withdraw: true after the owner agreed. Use this to recover unspent value from a prepaid card into the agent wallet.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to recover unspent value from a prepaid card into the agent wallet.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_connect
tools.title: Card provider verification status
tools.description: Whether the card provider needs the account holder to complete identity steps before cards can be bought. Use this before the first card purchase on an account; if steps are outstanding, get the link with agent_card_connect_link.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before the first card purchase on an account; if steps are outstanding, get the link with agent_card_connect_link.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: agent_card_connect_link
tools.title: Card provider verification link
tools.description: A browser link where the account holder completes the provider's identity steps. Give it to the owner; do not open it yourself. Use this when agent_card_connect reports identity steps still outstanding.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when agent_card_connect reports identity steps still outstanding.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: paired_markets
tools.title: List paired-coin markets
tools.description: Every asset a paired coin on Robinhood Chain can trade against, read live from the launchpad: tokenized stocks (NVDA, TSLA, SPY…), WETH, stablecoins and chain coins, each with its class, live USD price and the dollar market cap a pool in it opens at. Also returns the launch fee, swap fee and the creator's share of fees. Use this before paired_launch_quote to choose which markets a new coin should pair with.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before paired_launch_quote to choose which markets a new coin should pair with.

tools.name: paired_coins
tools.title: List paired coins
tools.description: Paired coins on Robinhood Chain, newest first, with every pool (quote asset, weight, price, dollar market cap, % sold), the verified descriptor and the three.ws agent that launched it. Pass agent_id for one agent's coins. Use this to browse launched paired coins; for one coin in full call paired_coin.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to browse launched paired coins; for one coin in full call paired_coin.

agent_id.description: Agent UUID (from list_my_agents).

tools.name: paired_coin
tools.title: Read a paired coin
