tools.name: list_agent_actions
tools.title: List an agent's action-provenance trail
tools.description: Read an agent's append-only action log, newest-first, cursor-paginated. Returns each action's id, type (e.g. launch, buy, post, reflect), payload, source_skill, created_at, and (when the action was signed) its ERC-191 signature + signer_address. Each record is checked against its own signature: `verification.reason` is `ok` (recovered signer matches the claimed address), `unsigned`, `signer_mismatch` (recovered a different address: tampering OR an action signed under a different canonical scheme; treat as unverified, not trusted), or `malformed_signature`. Pass the returned `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to page further. The ledger is owner-scoped: THREE_WS_TOKEN must own `agent_id`. Read-only; the log is immutable so older pages never change. Use this to audit what an agent did over time; to verify one action by id call query_action.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to audit what an agent did over time; to verify one action by id call query_action.

agent_id.description: The agent identity uuid whose provenance trail to read. Your token must own it.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor - pass the `next_cursor` from a previous call to fetch the next (older) page.

tools.name: query_action
tools.title: Fetch + verify one provenance action
tools.description: Fetch a single action from an agent's append-only log by its id, then verify it. Returns the action (type, payload, source_skill, created_at, signature, signer_address) plus a `verification` block: `signed`, `valid`, `reason` (`ok` | `unsigned` | `signer_mismatch` | `malformed_signature`), the `recovered` signer address, and the recomputed `digest`. `valid:true` means the ERC-191 signature recovers to the claimed signer over the canonical action form: cryptographic proof the named agent authored this exact action and it was not altered. The ledger is owner-scoped: THREE_WS_TOKEN must own `agent_id`. Returns ok:false / not_found when the id is absent from this agent's log. Use this to prove or check a single action someone cited; for the full trail call list_agent_actions. Read-only.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to prove or check a single action someone cited; for the full trail call list_agent_actions.

agent_id.description: The agent identity uuid that owns the action. Your token must own this agent.

id.description: The numeric action id to fetch (the `id` field from list_agent_actions).

tools.name: append_agent_action
tools.title: Append a signed action to the provenance ledger
tools.description: Record an action in an agent's append-only provenance ledger: the permanent, auditable trail of what the agent did. Provide `agent_id` (THREE_WS_TOKEN must own it), a short `type` (≤64 chars, e.g. launch, buy, post, reflect), an optional structured `payload`, and an optional `source_skill`. WRITE ACTION: this APPENDS a new immutable record: it can never be edited or deleted, and calling it twice records two distinct actions, so don't retry blindly. When an EVM signer is configured (THREE_WS_SIGNER_KEY env or the `signer_key` arg) the action is ERC-191-signed before sending, making its authorship publicly verifiable; with no key it is appended unsigned. Returns the stored record (with id + created_at) and a `signing` block reporting whether it was signed and by which address. Use this after an agent completes a real action worth auditing, once per action.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after an agent completes a real action worth auditing, once per action.

agent_id.description: The agent identity uuid to record the action under. Your token must own it.

type.description: Short action type, e.g. launch, buy, sell, post, reflect, follow. Truncated to 64 chars server-side.

payload.description: Structured details of the action (any JSON object) - e.g. { mint, amount_sol, signature }. Stored verbatim and covered by the signature.

source_skill.description: Identifier of the skill/tool that produced this action, for attribution in the trail.

signer_key.description: Optional 0x-prefixed EVM private key to ERC-191-sign this action. Overrides THREE_WS_SIGNER_KEY for this call. Omit to use the env key, or sign nothing if none is set.

tools.name: search_tokens
tools.title: Search Tokens
tools.description: Search pump.fun tokens by name, symbol, or mint address. Use this to find a coin's mint when you only know its name or ticker, then pass the mint to get_token_details or get_coin_intel.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find a coin's mint when you only know its name or ticker, then pass the mint to get_token_details or get_coin_intel.

tools.name: get_token_details
tools.title: Token Details
tools.description: Full details for a specific pump.fun token by mint address. Use this when you already have a mint and need its metadata, market cap, and curve status; for holder concentration call get_token_holders, for recent fills call get_token_trades.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you already have a mint and need its metadata, market cap, and curve status; for holder concentration call get_token_holders, for recent fills call get_token_trades.

tools.name: get_bonding_curve
tools.title: Bonding Curve
tools.description: Bonding curve analysis: real reserves, virtual reserves, and graduation progress (on-chain). Pre-graduation only: these reserves come from the pump program bonding-curve account, not from a PumpSwap pool. Pump renamed the quote-side fields on-chain (real_sol_reserves -> real_quote_reserves, virtual_sol_reserves -> virtual_quote_reserves) once a non-SOL quote asset became possible; the response keys below keep their original names and are still denominated in SOL, because the curve quote_mint is the SOL default on every coin created to date. A v3 buy that empties the curve completes it and buys the rest through a synthetic migration, priced on the reserves the PumpSwap pool will open with, so a large final buy is not capped at realTokenReserves. Once complete=true the curve is retired and pricing moves to the PumpSwap pool, so use pumpfun_quote_swap from that point on. Use this to read graduation progress or the curve spot price of a coin that has not graduated yet.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to read graduation progress or the curve spot price of a coin that has not graduated yet.

tools.name: get_token_trades
tools.title: Token Trades
tools.description: Recent buy/sell history for a token. Use this to read recent buy and sell flow on one coin; to see only large trades as they land, call pumpfun_watch_whales instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to read recent buy and sell flow on one coin; to see only large trades as they land, call pumpfun_watch_whales instead.

tools.name: get_trending_tokens
tools.title: Trending Tokens
tools.description: Top pump.fun tokens by market cap. Use this to scan the largest coins on pump.fun right now; for fresh launches call get_new_tokens, for coins that left the curve call get_graduated_tokens.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to scan the largest coins on pump.fun right now; for fresh launches call get_new_tokens, for coins that left the curve call get_graduated_tokens.

tools.name: get_new_tokens
tools.title: New Tokens

tools.whenToUse: Use this to catch launches in their first minutes; for the largest coins by market cap call get_trending_tokens instead.

tools.name: get_graduated_tokens

tools.whenToUse: Use this to list coins that now trade on a PumpSwap pool, where pumpfun_quote_swap applies instead of get_bonding_curve.

tools.name: pumpfun_list_claims
tools.title: List Creator Fee Claims
tools.description: List recent pump.fun fee-claim events for a creator wallet (on-chain, no indexer needed). Returns signature, mint, lamports, and Unix timestamp for each claim. Creator fees from the v3 curve and v2 pool trades wait on the curve and pool until a sweep_creator_fee moves them to the creator vault, so a claim covers only what was swept (usually in the same transaction) and fees still waiting appear in no claim yet. Use this to audit how much a creator has already cashed out; for only the claims inside a recent window call pumpfun_watch_claims.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to audit how much a creator has already cashed out; for only the claims inside a recent window call pumpfun_watch_claims.

tools.whenToUse: Use this to find which trader wallets are worth following; to see whether they hold a given coin, call get_coin_intel or get_token_holders.

tools.name: pumpfun_quote_swap
tools.title: Swap Quote (Read-Only)
tools.description: Read-only price quote for a pump.fun (PumpSwap) AMM swap on a GRADUATED coin. No signing or tx sending. One of inputMint/outputMint must be wSOL (So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112). Returns amountOut, priceImpactBps, route, expiresAtMs. Pricing follows PumpSwap exactly: the quote side is the EFFECTIVE reserve, pool_quote_token_account.amount + pool.virtual_quote_reserves (a SIGNED i128, commonly negative because PumpSwap v2 trades keep waiting protocol and creator fees in the vault and subtract them there), while the base side is the raw pool_base_token_account.amount, unchanged. Coins still on the bonding curve have no pool, so use get_bonding_curve instead. The quote is a snapshot: honour expiresAtMs and re-quote after it. Use this to size a trade on a graduated coin, or to measure its pool depth, before executing anywhere.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to size a trade on a graduated coin, or to measure its pool depth, before executing anywhere.

amountIn.description: Input amount in raw base units (lamports for SOL).

tools.name: social_x_post_impact
tools.title: X Post Price Impact
tools.description: Correlate an X (Twitter) post to a memecoin price impact. Fetches post metadata via oEmbed (no API key) and computes price delta from the pump.fun bonding curve in a ±windowMin window around the post. Use this to measure how one X post moved a coin that is still on its bonding curve (pricing is virtual_quote_reserves / virtual_token_reserves); a graduated coin has no curve, so the call fails rather than returning a zero price.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to measure how one X post moved a coin that is still on its bonding curve (pricing is virtual_quote_reserves / virtual_token_reserves); a graduated coin has no curve, so the call fails rather than returning a zero price.

mint.description: Solana token mint address (base58)

tools.whenToUse: Use this first when search_tokens, get_graduated_tokens, get_king_of_the_hill, or get_creator_profile fail or are missing, to see whether the indexer is configured and healthy.

tools.name: compose_scene
tools.title: Compose a 3D diorama plan from one sentence
tools.description: Compose a tiny 3D diorama from one short sentence. Returns a PLAN: an evocative title, a mood (dawn/day/dusk/night), ground + island type, a color palette, and 2-8 placed objects, each with a single-object forge prompt, position, scale and rotation. No meshes are generated yet and nothing is saved; feed the plan to the three.ws diorama page (or /api/forge per object) to build the world. Read-mostly but runs live LLM inference. Use this when you want to review or edit the plan, or forge the objects yourself; to get a finished GLB world in one call, use build_world instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you want to review or edit the plan, or forge the objects yourself; to get a finished GLB world in one call, use build_world instead.

prompt.description: One short sentence describing the world to build, e.g. "a lonely lighthouse on a stormy cliff".

Returns the orbitable viewer URL. Read-only. Use this when you already have a diorama id (from list_scenes or build_world) and need its objects, for example before passing them to export_scene.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you already have a diorama id (from list_scenes or build_world) and need its objects, for example before passing them to export_scene.

tools.title: List recent or featured dioramas

Returns a list of cards (id, title, mood, thumbnail/preview, view count) plus each world's viewer URL. Read-only. Use this to discover existing dioramas and their ids; fetch one in full with get_scene.

tools.name: export_scene
tools.title: Export a forged diorama as one GLB scene
tools.description: Merge an already-forged diorama (objects with real glbUrl values, e.g. from your own forging after compose_scene, or fetched via get_scene) into ONE glTF 2.0 binary: every object becomes a named, selectable node, plus a real ground disc and mood-tuned lighting. Returns the merged GLB URL and a ready-to-open three.ws Scene Studio link. Objects that never forged are skipped and reported rather than treated as a failure; a partial world still exports. Requires the target deployment to have object storage configured (three.ws does). Use this after every object in a diorama has a glbUrl and you want one downloadable GLB; to go from a sentence straight to the merged world, call build_world instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after every object in a diorama has a glbUrl and you want one downloadable GLB; to go from a sentence straight to the merged world, call build_world instead.

tools.name: build_world
tools.title: Build a complete 3D world from one sentence (no browser needed)
tools.description: One sentence → a fully forged, exported 3D world, entirely server-side: composes the scene plan, forges every object on the free text→3D lane, and merges the result into one GLB with named, selectable nodes plus ground and lighting. Returns the populated diorama, the merged GLB URL, and a ready-to-open Scene Studio link. This is the whole progressive /diorama browser flow collapsed into one call; it can take a couple of minutes for a full object set. Partial forges are not failures: whatever forged is exported, and `skipped` names anything that did not. Use this when you want a finished world from one sentence with no intermediate steps; to inspect or adjust the plan before anything is forged, call compose_scene instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you want a finished world from one sentence with no intermediate steps; to inspect or adjust the plan before anything is forged, call compose_scene instead.

prompt.description: One short sentence describing the world to build, e.g. "a neon alley with a food cart and two streetlights".

tools.name: list_signal_feeds
tools.title: Browse the signal-feed marketplace
tools.description: Discover copy-trade signal feeds on three.ws. Returns the public directory of active feeds, each ranked by its PROVEN realized edge (hit-rate × realized ROI, confidence-regressed toward the publisher's verified track-record score until enough signals have closed - a thin feed riding one lucky call can never top a deep, consistent one). For each feed you get its numeric `id` (pass this to subscribe_signal), `slug`, title, the publisher (name, verified badge, track-record score, realized SOL P&L), pricing (per-signal and per-epoch USDC), and proven stats (closed signals, hit-rate, average realized %, active subscribers, executed fills, avg emit→fill latency, avg follower ROI). Sort by `edge` (default), `roi`, `hitrate`, `subscribers`, or `newest`. Public, read-only live data; no key required. Use this to choose a feed before subscribe_signal; to rank the publishers themselves call get_mirror_leaderboard.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to choose a feed before subscribe_signal; to rank the publishers themselves call get_mirror_leaderboard.

network.description: Solana network the feeds publish on (default mainnet).

sort.description: Ranking key: edge (proven realized edge, default), roi (avg realized %), hitrate, subscribers, or newest.

tools.name: get_mirror_leaderboard
tools.title: Rank signal publishers by realized performance
tools.description: Rank followable agents (signal publishers / copy-trade leaders) by REAL, on-chain-derived performance - never inflated. Every number traces to a real signature: realized P&L and win-rate come from closed sniper round-trips, volume from the discretionary custody ledger, and losers are included. Each leader returns rank, agent_id, name, avatar, settled trades, wins, win_rate, realized pnl_sol, roi_pct, trade count, volume_sol, follower counts, last trade time, and a composite score (realized ROI weighted by sample size so a one-trade fluke cannot top a consistent trader). Sort by `score` (default), `pnl`, `followers`, `volume`, or `winrate`. Use this to find a leader before subscribing to their feed. Public, read-only live data - no key required.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to find a leader before subscribing to their feed.

network.description: Solana network to rank on (default mainnet).

sort.description: Ranking key: score (default), pnl, followers, volume, or winrate.

tools.name: get_subscriptions
tools.title: List your signal subscriptions + delivery history
tools.description: List every signal subscription owned by the authenticated account - the follower's tracking surface. Each subscription returns its numeric `id` (pass this to set_subscription_status), the subscriber agent, the feed it follows (slug, title, publisher, pricing), the copy-trade config (mode simulate/live, billing, base_sol, size_scaling, max_per_trade_sol, slippage_bps, firewall_level, copy_exits), live status (status, killed flag, epoch_paid_until, last delivered emission), and the realized delivery stats: `stats.executed` (mirror fills that executed on-chain), `stats.paid_count` (paid deliveries), and `stats.usdc_spent` (total USDC paid to the publisher). Use this to check what you follow and what it has cost before changing a subscription with set_subscription_status. Requires THREE_WS_API_KEY. Read-only live data.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to check what you follow and what it has cost before changing a subscription with set_subscription_status.

tools.name: subscribe_signal
tools.title: Subscribe an agent to a signal feed
tools.description:
Subscribe one of YOUR agents to a signal feed so it copy-trades the publisher. Idempotent: a feed is keyed by (subscriber agent, feed) - re-calling updates the existing subscription instead of creating a duplicate. A new subscription starts at the current emission head, so it is never charged for or made to mirror signals emitted before it subscribed.

PAYMENT & RISK: `mode:"simulate"` (default) mirrors WITHOUT paying or trading - it sizes and labels the orders for trust-building, spends nothing. `mode:"live"` BOTH pays the publisher in USDC (x402, per-signal or per-epoch per the feed pricing) AND auto-mirrors real on-chain trades from the subscriber agent's custodial wallet, within its spend policy. Money moves at delivery time (when the publisher emits a signal), not at the moment you call this tool. Use set_subscription_status with killed:true to halt all further pay/trade instantly. Requires THREE_WS_API_KEY; the agent must be owned by that account. Use this after picking a feed with list_signal_feeds; start in simulate mode and switch to live only on the owner's explicit say-so.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after picking a feed with list_signal_feeds; start in simulate mode and switch to live only on the owner's explicit say-so.

agent_id.description: ID of the subscriber agent (must be owned by the authenticated account). This agent pays and mirrors.

feed_id.description: Numeric feed id to follow (from list_signal_feeds - the `id` field). The feed must be active.

mode.description: simulate = no pay, no trade (default, safe). live = pays USDC AND auto-mirrors real trades.

billing.description: How live mode is charged: per_signal (each entry) or per_epoch (a flat fee per epoch window).

base_sol.description: Base order size in SOL before the per-signal size multiple/scaling (0.001 - 10, default 0.05).

size_scaling.description: Multiplier applied on top of the base size (0.01 - 20, default 1).

max_per_trade_sol.description: Hard cap on any single mirrored order in SOL (0.001 - 50, default 0.25).

slippage_bps.description: Max slippage in basis points for mirrored trades (0 - 5000, default 300 = 3%).

firewall_level.description: Risk firewall on mirrored buys: block (refuse risky trades, default) or warn (allow with a flag).

copy_exits.description: Mirror the publisher's exits too (sell when they sell). Default true.

tools.name: set_subscription_status
tools.title: Resume, pause, stop, or kill a subscription
tools.description:
Control an existing signal subscription owned by the authenticated account.
  • active  - (re)activate it; this also CLEARS any kill flag so it resumes paying/mirroring.
  • paused  - stop delivering for now; the kill flag (if set) is left untouched.
  • stopped - stop the subscription (soft - its delivery history is kept).
  • killed  - INSTANT kill switch: halts everything immediately; the kill is honoured before any payment or trade can fire. Use this to stop a live subscription from spending or trading right now.
Idempotent - setting the same state again is a no-op. Get the subscription `id` from get_subscriptions. Requires THREE_WS_API_KEY.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to stop a live subscription from spending or trading right now.

state.description: Target state: active (resume + clear kill), paused, stopped, or killed (instant halt of all pay/trade).

tools.name: decode_solana_memo_data_uri
tools.title: Decode a Solana memo data URI
tools.description: Decode and validate one base64 image data URI from a Solana memo. Only PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF are accepted. The bytes stay local to the MCP process, are checked against their claimed file signature, and return inline as an MCP image with byte length, SHA-256, and dimensions when available. Use this when you already hold a data URI string; to pull media from a transaction call extract_solana_memo_media instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you already hold a data URI string; to pull media from a transaction call extract_solana_memo_media instead.

dataUri.description: A complete base64 image data URI from an SPL Memo instruction.

tools.name: extract_solana_memo_media
tools.title: Extract media from a Solana transaction memo
tools.description: Fetch a confirmed Solana transaction (legacy, v0, or v1), inspect top-level and inner SPL Memo instructions, and render every supported embedded image data URI inline. The response identifies the source signature, fee payer, slot, and transaction version, and reports rejected media without returning unsafe bytes. This is chain data, not a claim of authorship or safety. Use this when you have a transaction signature; to scan an address for media call find_solana_memo_media.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you have a transaction signature; to scan an address for media call find_solana_memo_media.

tools.name: find_solana_memo_media
tools.title: Find recent memo media for a Solana address
tools.description: Scan a Solana address's recent confirmed transactions and return only validated image data URIs carried by SPL Memo instructions. Signatures whose memo summary holds no data URI are skipped without fetching the transaction, so a scan costs one RPC call plus one per candidate. Pass a memo program id as the address to watch every memo written to it. Use the returned signatures to verify provenance in an explorer. Use this when you have an address but no signature; for one known transaction call extract_solana_memo_media.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you have an address but no signature; for one known transaction call extract_solana_memo_media.

address.description: Solana wallet, token account, or program address in base58.

limit.description: Recent signatures to scan, from 1 to 1000 (default 100).

before.description: Continue the scan from signatures older than this one (the previous response's next_before).

tools.name: get_solana_memo_media_status
tools.title: Solana memo media capability
tools.description: Report the local decoding policy, recognized memo programs, and ordered Solana RPC failover hosts. No network call is made and no data is stored. Use this to check which RPC hosts and memo programs the server will use before a scan.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to check which RPC hosts and memo programs the server will use before a scan.

Read-only, no signer or payment required. Use this to quote $THREE in USD or size a USD amount in $THREE; for a wallet's holdings call three_balance.

tools.name: three_balance
tools.title: Read a wallet's $THREE + SOL balance
tools.description: Return the $THREE and SOL balance for a Solana pubkey. If no pubkey is given, uses the configured signer (SOLANA_SECRET_KEY). Read-only, no payment. Use this to check holdings before a three_burn or to confirm a wallet holds $THREE.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to check holdings before a three_burn or to confirm a wallet holds $THREE.

pubkey.description: Base58 pubkey to read. Defaults to the configured signer's address.

tools.name: three_burn
tools.title: Burn $THREE on-chain (incinerator + treasury split)
tools.description: Burn a USD-denominated amount of the $THREE your wallet holds. Quotes USD→$THREE via Jupiter, then sends ONE Solana transaction that splits it between the incinerator (burn) and the three.ws treasury, per the live public token config. EXECUTION ACTION. Signs and broadcasts on Solana mainnet, IRREVERSIBLE: pass confirm:true. Capped by MAX_BURN_USD. The resolved mint is asserted to be canonical $THREE before signing. Requires a signer (SOLANA_SECRET_KEY env or the `secret` arg) holding enough $THREE. Returns the tx signature, the burned/treasury breakdown, and a Solscan link. Use this when the person explicitly asks to burn and has approved the USD amount; check three_balance first.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the person explicitly asks to burn and has approved the USD amount; check three_balance first.

usd.description: USD value of $THREE to burn (priced live via Jupiter).

burnBps.description: Share routed to the incinerator in basis points. Default 5000 (50% burn / 50% treasury). 10000 = burn everything.

memo.description: Optional note appended to the on-chain memo.

secret.description: Base58 signer override. Defaults to SOLANA_SECRET_KEY. Treat like cash.

confirm.description: Must be true to execute this irreversible burn (when REQUIRE_CONFIRM is on).

tools.title: Get avatar embed code
tools.description: Get a ready-to-paste iframe that embeds a live, interactive three.ws 3D avatar into any website or app, as easy as embedding a YouTube video. Use this when the avatar has to live on a page outside this chat; to show it here, call render_avatar instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the avatar has to live on a page outside this chat; to show it here, call render_avatar instead.

id.description: Avatar UUID (from a three.ws avatar URL or get_avatar).

model.description: Direct GLB/GLTF model URL (skips lookup; used as-is).

tools.name: get_avatar
tools.title: Get avatar metadata
tools.description: Fetch metadata for a three.ws avatar (name, GLB model url, owner, visibility) by id or @handle. Use this to resolve a handle to its avatar id and GLB url before rendering, embedding, or downloading it.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to resolve a handle to its avatar id and GLB url before rendering, embedding, or downloading it.

id.description: Avatar UUID (from a three.ws avatar URL or get_avatar).

tools.name: load_session
tools.title: Load a tutoring session ledger
tools.description: Read the running tab for a Pay-As-You-Learn tutoring session by its sessionId. Returns the itemized ledger: one lineItem per answered question (question text, level, output tokens, per-item cost in USDC atomics and a "$x.xxxxxx" string, and the timestamp), plus the session status ("open" | "closed"), questionCount, and the running totalAtomics / totalUsd. If the session was already closed it also returns the finalized, attested invoice. A sessionId with no stored history returns an empty open session (questionCount 0) rather than an error; that is an honest "nothing billed yet", not a failure. Viewing the tab is always free; this never charges the learner. Use this to show the learner what they owe so far; to seal the invoice call close_session. Read-only live data.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to show the learner what they owe so far; to seal the invoice call close_session.

sessionId.description: Opaque tutoring session identifier (the id the session was opened with). Truncated to 100 chars by the API.

tools.name: close_session
tools.title: Close a tutoring session (finalize invoice)
tools.description: Finalize a Pay-As-You-Learn tutoring session and return its itemized, attested invoice. Seals the ledger for the given sessionId: status flips to "closed", a SHA-256 attestation is stamped over the line items and total, and no further questions can be billed to this session afterward. Returns sessionId, createdAt, closedAt, questionCount, the full lineItems array, the totalAtomics / totalUsd owed, and the attestation hash. Closing itself is FREE and moves no funds: the learner was already charged per answered question; this only produces the final receipt. Idempotent: closing an already-closed session returns the same total. Use this when the learner is done; call load_session first to review the tab before sealing it.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when the learner is done; call load_session first to review the tab before sealing it.

sessionId.description: Opaque tutoring session identifier to finalize. Truncated to 100 chars by the API.

tools.name: vanity_quote
tools.title: Quote the bounty price for a vanity pattern
tools.description: Quote how hard a Solana vanity address is and what to escrow for it. Give a Base58 prefix and/or suffix and get the expected attempts, rarity tier, and an honest suggested USDC bounty (atomic units) from the difficulty→price oracle. Pure function of the pattern - no wallet, no payment, fully read-only. Use this before posting a grind-bounty so you escrow a fair amount.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before posting a grind-bounty so you escrow a fair amount.

prefix.description: Base58 prefix the address must start with (e.g. "THREE").

suffix.description: Base58 suffix the address must end with.

ignoreCase.description: Match the pattern case-insensitively (cheaper, less rare). Default false.

tools.name: vanity_appraise
tools.title: Appraise the rarity of a Solana address
tools.description: Appraise how rare a Solana address is: its detected vanity pattern, rarity score, rarity bits, tier, and expected grind attempts. Pure math on the Base58 address; nothing is stored. If the address has been published to the proof-of-grind gallery, the public entry is returned too. Use this to rate an address someone already has; to price grinding a new pattern call vanity_quote. Read-only, no payment.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to rate an address someone already has; to price grinding a new pattern call vanity_quote.

address.description: The Base58 Solana public key to appraise (32 - 44 chars).

prefixLen.description: Override how many leading characters to treat as the pattern prefix.

suffixLen.description: Override how many trailing characters to treat as the pattern suffix.

tools.name: vanity_board
tools.title: Browse the vanity grind-bounty board
tools.description: Browse the public grind-bounty board: vanity-address bounties requesters have escrowed for the worker fleet to grind. Filter by status (open / all / settled), sort by recency, reward, or expiry, and paginate. Each bounty shows its pattern, USDC amount, difficulty, status, and timing. Use this to see what bounties exist and what they pay; workers looking for claimable work should call vanity_open. Read-only; posting a bounty is a separate x402-paid write on the HTTP API.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to see what bounties exist and what they pay; workers looking for claimable work should call vanity_open.

status.description: Which bounties to list. Default open.

sort.description: Order: newest first, biggest reward first, or soonest to expire. Default recency.

tools.name: vanity_open
tools.title: List claimable open bounties for workers
tools.description: List the open, unexpired bounties a grinding worker can race to claim: the queue worker fleets poll. Each entry carries the pattern to grind and the escrowed USDC reward; the first worker to submit a verified, sealed key wins. Use this when running a grinding worker that needs its next job; for the full board with settled bounties call vanity_board. Read-only discovery; submitting a claim is a separate write on the HTTP API.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when running a grinding worker that needs its next job; for the full board with settled bounties call vanity_board.

limit.description: Max claimable bounties to return (1 - 100, default 30).

tools.name: vanity_stats
tools.title: Live grind-bounty market totals
tools.description: Get live totals for the grind-bounty market: how many bounties are open, how much USDC is currently escrowed, and how much has been paid out to winning workers. A quick pulse on market activity. Use this for a one-line market summary; for individual bounties call vanity_board. Read-only, no params.
tools.whenToUse: Use this for a one-line market summary; for individual bounties call vanity_board.

tools.name: vanity_leaderboard
tools.title: Top grinders by USDC earned
tools.description: Rank the worker fleet: the top grinders by total USDC earned from winning vanity-address bounties. Each entry shows a worker id and its cumulative payout. Use this to see who is winning bounties; for market totals call vanity_stats. Read-only.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to see who is winning bounties; for market totals call vanity_stats.

limit.description: How many top grinders to return (1 - 100, default 10).

tools.name: vanity_config
tools.title: Bounty market config: payout + asset metadata
tools.description: Read the grind-bounty market configuration: whether on-chain payouts are configured (can a winner actually be paid?), the settlement asset (USDC) and its decimals, which escrow networks are live (Base / Solana), the pricing band (floor + max atomics), the bounty protocol version, and the sealed-envelope scheme. Call this before posting a bounty to confirm the market can pay out. Read-only, no params.
tools.whenToUse: Call this before posting a bounty to confirm the market can pay out.

tools.name: vanity_gallery
tools.title: Browse the proof-of-grind rarity gallery
tools.description: Browse the public proof-of-grind gallery: rare Solana addresses people have published with a verifiable grind receipt. Sort by rarity score or recency, filter by tier, minimum pattern length, or a substring the pattern must contain, and paginate. Each entry shows the address, pattern, rarity score/bits, tier, and an explorer link. Use this to browse published rare addresses; to score one address call vanity_appraise. Read-only.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to browse published rare addresses; to score one address call vanity_appraise.

sort.description: Order by rarity score (rarest first) or recency. Default score.

tier.description: Filter to a single rarity tier id.

minLength.description: Only patterns at least this many characters long.

contains.description: Only addresses whose vanity pattern contains this substring.

tools.name: analyze_image
tools.title: Analyze an image against a prompt
tools.description: Let the agent SEE an image and answer a question about it. Supply the image as `imageUrl` (a public https URL the vision server fetches) OR `image` (raw base64 / a data: URI), and a `prompt` describing what to extract - e.g. "What objects are in this scene?", "Read the text in this screenshot", "Is this avatar render rigged correctly?". Returns the model's answer as `text`, plus the `provider` and `model` that served it (a free NVIDIA NIM lane when available, an automatic paid backstop otherwise - the caller never pays). Analysis only: it does not store or mutate anything. Accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, or GIF up to 12 MB; base64 inputs are size-checked before upload. Use this when you have a specific question about an image; for a general caption or alt text with no question, call describe_image instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when you have a specific question about an image; for a general caption or alt text with no question, call describe_image instead.

prompt.description: The question or instruction about the image (what to extract, read, classify, or critique).

imageUrl.description: Public https URL of the image to analyze. Provide this OR `image`, not both.

image.description: The image as raw base64 or a `data:image/...;base64,...` URI. Provide this OR `imageUrl`, not both.

imageType.description: MIME type of a raw base64 `image` (ignored for data URIs / `imageUrl`). Defaults to image/jpeg.

maxTokens.description: Maximum tokens in the answer (16 - 2048). Higher = longer, more detailed reads. Default 512.

tools.name: describe_image
tools.title: Describe an image in natural language
tools.description: Get a plain-language description of an image - ideal for alt text, captions, or a quick "what is this?" read when you have no specific question. Supply the image as `imageUrl` (a public https URL) OR `image` (raw base64 / data: URI). Use `detail` to pick brief / standard / detailed, and `focus` to steer the description toward something specific (e.g. "the clothing", "any visible text"). Returns the prose as `description`, plus the `provider` and `model` that served it (free NVIDIA NIM first, automatic paid backstop otherwise, so the caller never pays). Read-only; accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, or GIF up to 12 MB. Use this for alt text or a caption when you have no particular question; to ask something specific about the image, call analyze_image instead.
tools.whenToUse: Use this for alt text or a caption when you have no particular question; to ask something specific about the image, call analyze_image instead.

imageUrl.description: Public https URL of the image to describe. Provide this OR `image`, not both.

image.description: The image as raw base64 or a `data:image/...;base64,...` URI. Provide this OR `imageUrl`, not both.

imageType.description: MIME type of a raw base64 `image` (ignored for data URIs / `imageUrl`). Defaults to image/jpeg.

detail.description: How much description to return: brief (one sentence), standard (2 - 3 sentences), or detailed (a full paragraph).

focus.description: Optional aspect to emphasize in the description (e.g. "any visible text", "the background", "the pose").

tools.name: get_vision_status
tools.title: Vision availability + accepted formats
tools.description: Check whether the three.ws vision pipeline is live on the target deployment and which image formats it accepts. Returns `configured` (true when at least one VLM provider - a free NVIDIA NIM lane or the paid backstop - can serve a request) and `image_types` (the accepted MIME types). Use this before calling analyze_image / describe_image so the agent can decide whether to offer a "describe this image" action. No image, no key, no cost.
tools.whenToUse: Use this before calling analyze_image / describe_image so the agent can decide whether to offer a "describe this image" action.

tools.name: x402_wallet
tools.title: The agent's x402 spending wallet (address + balance)
tools.description: Show a Solana wallet's address and live SOL + USDC balance. With no `address`, derives the wallet from the configured signer (SOLANA_SECRET_KEY). Call this before pay_and_call to confirm there's USDC to spend. Read-only; never moves funds.
tools.whenToUse: Call this before pay_and_call to confirm there's USDC to spend.

address.description: Base58 Solana address to inspect. Omit to use the configured signer wallet.

tools.name: find_services
tools.title: Find paid x402 services the agent can call
tools.description: Search the live x402 facilitator network (PayAI + Coinbase CDP bazaar) for paid services (HTTP APIs and MCP tools). Returns each match with its price, networks, and resource URL. Use this when a task needs a paid API or tool you do not already have; to use a match, check its price with inspect_endpoint, then pass its resource into pay_and_call. Read-only.
tools.whenToUse: Use this when a task needs a paid API or tool you do not already have; to use a match, check its price with inspect_endpoint, then pass its resource into pay_and_call.

query.description: What you need, e.g. "weather", "image upscale", "token intel".

network.description: CAIP-2 network filter, e.g. "solana:*" or "eip155:8453".

max_price_usdc.description: Only return services at or under this USDC price.

tools.name: inspect_endpoint
tools.title: Inspect an x402 endpoint (price + requirements, no payment)
tools.description: Fetch an x402 endpoint and return its 402 payment requirements - every accepted scheme, network, asset, price and pay-to address - WITHOUT paying. If the endpoint is free, returns its result instead. No signer required. Use this to learn the cost before pay_and_call.
tools.whenToUse: Use this to learn the cost before pay_and_call.

url.description: The x402 endpoint URL to inspect.

body.description: JSON body for a POST probe.

tools.name: pay_and_call
tools.title: Pay an x402 endpoint in USDC or $THREE and return its result
tools.description:
Call a paid x402 endpoint and settle the payment automatically, then return the result. Use this after inspect_endpoint has shown the price and the user has approved paying it; a settled payment cannot be undone.

Two modes:
• Self-custodial (default): signs with SOLANA_SECRET_KEY or `secret` arg; you hold the key.
• Session-governed: pass `session_token` (a three.ws Payment Session token); the platform wallet signs on your behalf; the session's budget, allowlist, and per-tx cap are enforced by the platform. No private key required. Supports Solana USDC and Base USDC sessions.

Pay in USDC (default) or, when the endpoint advertises it, in $THREE (set token:"three"). Bounded by max_usd and the MAX_PAY_USD cap; refuses before any money moves if the price is over the cap. With REQUIRE_CONFIRM on, the call refuses until re-issued with confirm:true.
tools.whenToUse: Use this after inspect_endpoint has shown the price and the user has approved paying it; a settled payment cannot be undone.

url.description: The x402 endpoint to pay and call.

session_token.description: three.ws Payment Session token (pss_…). When provided, the platform wallet pays - no local key needed. Overrides `secret`.

token.description: Settlement token. "usdc" (default) or "three" - the $THREE platform token; the endpoint must advertise it. Ignored when session_token is set.

max_usd.description: Hard ceiling for THIS call in USD. Can only lower the MAX_PAY_USD cap, never raise it.

secret.description: Per-call base58 signer override (defaults to SOLANA_SECRET_KEY). Ignored when session_token is set.

confirm.description: Must be true to execute when REQUIRE_CONFIRM is on.

idempotency_key.description: Deduplication key for this call. Recommended when using session_token to avoid double-charges on retries.
